script: How much does the Shaedon Sharpe injury actually HURT Portland, or does it LOWKEY HELP? Shaedon Sharpe just tore the meniscus in his right knee, and he's expected to miss about six months, which is brutal timing because he's only 23 years old and just wrapped up the best season of his career, averaging 20.8 points a game for the Portland Trail Blazers. But the six months on the sidelines is the part everyone will forget about a year from now. This is another major leg injury for a guy who has struggled to stay healthy, since last season he missed a huge chunk of games with a stress fracture in his other leg, and before that he needed surgery for a core muscle injury. So for a player Portland just handed a 4 year, 90 million dollar contract, that history is a real worry. But that worry is exactly why the reaction to this injury has been so strange. Portland's roster was already jammed before this, because over the offseason they traded for Ja Morant and got Damian Lillard back healthy, so when you add in Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson, you've suddenly got four quality guards all fighting for minutes at basically two spots, and Sharpe was already getting pushed to the bench. So even though losing a 20 point scorer hurts, several writers are quietly calling it a silver lining, because with Sharpe out, that logjam clears up on its own. Lillard and Morant can start, with Holiday and Henderson backing them up, and the new coach finally has a rotation that actually makes sense.
